key_insight: PatientAgentBench shows that patient-facing health AI agents can look strong in static QA but still make serious mistakes in realistic, tool-using conversations.
clinical_relevance: For primary care and triage, the benchmark highlights safety, workflow, and escalation failures that matter when an AI agent may act on behalf of a patient.
method: Built a patient-facing agent benchmark with a foundation model wrapped in healthcare tools and a simulated patient.
Scored conversations with an LLM-as-a-Jury across six clinician-grounded dimensions.
Validated the jury against licensed clinician annotations on shared conversations.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated 10 models across 1,200 scenarios and found triage pass rates ranging from 32% to 88%, with strongest models still imperfect overall.
watch_item: Because the benchmark depends on simulated patients, tool environments, and LLM-based scoring, real-world deployment still requires careful clinical oversight and external validation.
paper_title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
